title: Config
description:
A parsed `arch.config.json`, before `extends` is resolved and before globs
and regexes are compiled.

$schema.description:
The `$schema` URL. Present so editors offer completion; archwarden
itself ignores it.

root.description:
Where globs resolve from. Defaults to the config file's directory.

A preset may not set this: it cannot know the layout of the repository
including it, and silently relocating every glob in a config is not
something a shared package should be able to do.

extends.description:
Presets to inherit from. A `./`-prefixed entry is a path; anything else
is an npm package name.

ignore.description:
Extra ignore globs, on top of `.gitignore`, which is always honoured.

Ignore always wins over a rule's scope, however specific that scope is:
a kill-switch that can be overridden by accident is not one.

modules.description: Rules grouped under a label, which is what findings report in brackets.

rules.description:
Rules belonging to no module, typically import boundaries, which are
cross-module by nature. They report as `[*]`.

disable.description:
Rule ids inherited from a preset that this config drops.

Without this, one unwanted rule makes a whole preset unusable.

OneOrMany.description:
One `T`, or several.

Serialises back to whichever shape it was written in, so a config that
round-trips through archwarden does not gain array brackets it never had.

anyOf.description: Several values, written as an array.

SkipDirs.description: Which directories are exempt, and from what.

prefixes.description: Directory name prefixes. Empty disables the escape hatch.

globs.description: Globs, for cases a prefix cannot express.

oneOf.description:
Exempt from `structure` rules only. Files inside are still parsed and
still enter the import graph.

Removed from the walk entirely, and therefore invisible to every rule.

Rarely what you want: it turns `mkdir _x && mv offender.ts _x/` into a
way to bypass any import boundary. `config doctor` warns when this is
combined with `import-boundary` rules.

Module.description:
A named group of rules.

A module is a label, not a scope: it exists so a finding can say
`[domain] packages/domain/src/user/wrong-folder`. Each rule still carries
its own scope.

ModuleId.description: A module's identifier. Modules are labels for grouping output, not scopes.

Rule.description:
One rule, discriminated by `type`.

`import-boundary` is an ordinary rule like the rest. There is no `graph`
key: boundaries go through the same matcher and the same
`describe_expectation`, which is what keeps `describe` and `agent-guide` in
lockstep with the checker. See decision 14.

oneOf.description: Which folders may exist, and which filenames.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across the config and its presets.

roots.description: Directory globs this rule applies to.

warn_subfolders.description:
Subdirectory names that are permitted but reported as warnings,
whatever `level` says. Naming a folder is more specific than the rule's
blanket severity, and the more specific declaration wins.

recurse_into.description: Subdirectories that carry the same structural contract, recursively.

filename_patterns.description: Regexes every direct child file's name must match at least one of.

oneOf.description: The filename dictates the exported symbol's name.

roots.description: Directory globs this rule applies to.

file_pattern.description: Regex over the filename, with a named capture group.

must_export.description: The export the file must carry.

oneOf.description: Every unit file needs a spec sibling.

roots.description: Directory globs this rule applies to.

subfolders.description: Subdirectories subject to the rule. `["."]` means the scope itself.

spec_markers.description:
What makes a filename a spec: `spec`, `test`, or both.

A marker, not a whole suffix: the extension is taken from the source
file, so `Component.tsx` wants `Component.spec.tsx` without anyone
saying so. The default accepts both markers, which is what vitest and
jest do, so the common project needs no configuration here at all.

require_non_empty_spec.description:
Whether the spec must contain at least one `it(...)` or `test(...)`.
A bare `describe(...)` does not count: an empty describe block
satisfies the letter of the rule while defeating its purpose.

oneOf.description: Layer A may not import from layer B.

from.description: Directory globs selecting the importer. Same semantics as `roots`.

forbid_import_from.description:
Globs matched against the *resolved* import path. Matching means the
import is illegal.

must_import_from.description:
Globs matched against the resolved import path. If none of the file's
imports match, the file is illegal.

except.description: Exceptions, also matched against the resolved path.

include_type_only.description: Whether `import type` and inline `type` marks count.

oneOf.description: Files matching a pattern must call a given symbol.

roots.description: Directory globs this rule applies to.

must_call.description: The call the file must contain.

RuleId.description: A rule's stable identifier, unique across a config and its presets.

Level.description: How seriously a finding is taken.

oneOf.description:
Reported and visible, but the run still succeeds. For technical debt
that must stay in sight until it is paid down.

kind.description:
Declaration forms that satisfy the rule: one name, a list of names, or
`"any"`. See the table in `docs/RULES.md`.

name.description: The required name, as a template over `file_pattern`'s capture groups.

signature_hint.description:
A signature shown by `scaffold`. **Never verified** — constraining the
type of an export is type checking, which is `tsc`'s job.

symbol.description:
The callee as it appears at a call site, e.g. `Event.save`. Method
chains are matched exactly.

imported_from.description:
The module the symbol must be imported from, which disambiguates
same-named functions from different packages.
